applicability.rationale: All four files are in the owned continuous-recovery exact-tag workflow and directly produce, publish, or validate its evidence artifacts.

confidence.rationale: The exact patch, base, four after-images, call graph, schema changes, privacy functions, and a concrete in-memory coordinated-drift counterexample were independently inspected. Missing runtime evidence does not affect the established need to revise.

impact.rationale: The patch changes only the isolated continuous-recovery test/report pipeline, but it changes a public evidence schema and the metadata used to demonstrate real bearer-role/RBAC behavior. A wrong mapping can make security evidence semantically false even though product authorization remains enforced.

checker validate_http -> schema-v2 report and index comparison

materialBoundaries.counterexample: A caller-supplied independent role and actor could disagree and publish false evidence.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Every one of the 31 CASE names selects exactly one real authz.Role and one public CASE_ACTOR, and unknown input fails before token access or network dispatch.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: call no longer accepts either value; the exact CASE selector returns both, default returns false, and selection precedes token lookup and http.Client.Do.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Treating CASE_ACTOR as an allowed secret could expose a real private value equal to that literal.
materialBoundaries.invariant: No raw private role is deliberately emitted, and no role/actor exception, mask, or encoding bypass weakens the original secret fence.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Report and index use caseActor, while independent function hashes show private_bases, write_private, append_jsonl, encoded_secret_variants, build_forbidden, report_diagnostic_status, fence_outputs, capture, and main unchanged; collision negatives still reject every actor encoding.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Swap FIRST_UNKNOWN_CREATE to APPROVER and FIRST_UNKNOWN_APPROVE to ADMIN in reader, worker, and Go selector. Counts, inspect-role assertions, policy snippets, call count, and the current observed-versus-expected check all remain satisfied.
materialBoundaries.invariant: The MODEL independently defines correct CASE-to-role semantics instead of accepting coordinated producer and reader drift.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Use a separate immutable 31-entry expected CASE-to-authz.Role/CASE_ACTOR map in the MODEL, then compare Go selector, reader table, and worker table independently to it; add the coordinated swap as a negative.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: A stale v1 producer or mixed v1/v2 index could break artifact acceptance or silently omit fields.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Report v2 and index v2 are produced, fenced, and accepted together without dropping any of the 31 HTTP cases or old validation gates.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: All three source paths require exact v2 schemas and exact row keys; the reader retains all response-body, path, digest, status, and state-chain checks.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: Go report producer, worker public artifacts, and Python reader

materialBoundaries.counterexample: A report with outcome FAIL after HTTP 26 and a real 503 has fewer than 31 rows and a non-success status. The new len(rows)==31 and status==want/errorClass==NONE checks raise before REPORT_AND_HTTP_OUTPUTS fencing, private fsync receipts, the final fence, and public evidence writes.
materialBoundaries.invariant: A failed real HTTPS run must retain its safely fenced, source-bound observed HTTP prefix and fixed diagnostic rather than being rejected before export; final acceptance must still require all 31 successes.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Split evidence capture from acceptance: for PASS require the exact 31 successful rows; for FAIL allow only an ordered 0..31 prefix with exact CASE/actor/method/path identity and the producer's closed status/errorClass/body-observation shapes, fence every observed byte twice, and still let the independent reader/fresh acceptance require 31 successes.

recoverability.rationale: The change is confined to four test/CI evidence files, adds no migration or persisted product state, and can be reverted as one isolated patch.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The runtime selector and privacy removal are narrow, but the claimed independent source binding has a demonstrated coordinated-drift counterexample. In addition, safe_report_outputs now requires a complete successful 31-row report before either fence/export path, so real partial failure evidence is lost. Go compilation, formatting, and exact-tag Linux execution have not run.

regressionProtection.rationale: Six Python MODEL tests pass and catch single-sided drift, report mutation, schemas, privacy collisions, and source bindings. They neither reject a coordinated CASE actor swap across reader, worker, and Go selector nor exercise safe_report_outputs with a valid partial FAIL prefix.

riskDrivers: safe_report_outputs became success-only and rejects partial FAIL prefixes before the privacy fence and artifact export
MODEL expected CASE-to-role map is derived from the mutable reader table rather than an independent fixed source contract

statusQuoRisk.rationale: The current raw role metadata collides with the unchanged private-secret fence and blocks publication of otherwise successful continuous-recovery evidence. The failure is fail-closed rather than a demonstrated secret disclosure.
